“Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.” Interpreted through the New Keynesian/DSGE lens (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler 1999; Woodford), the FOMC’s commitment to keep the policy rate at 0–0.25% and to average inflation targeting reflects a systematic, Taylor‑rule‑consistent approach that anchors expectations while “looking through” transitory inflation pressures. Concurrent balance‑sheet expansion and money‑market operations (IOER at 0.15%, ON RRP at 0.05%) support the credit channel (Bernanke–Gertler) and ensure effective floor‑system control of short rates, reinforcing accommodative financial conditions. Given the positive growth signals and policy support, but with explicit acknowledgement of residual risks and sectoral weakness (and Orphanides‑style real‑time uncertainty), the overall tone is moderately positive rather than exuberant.
